$comment: LP FIDELITY LEDGER. Each entry is a geometric quantity measured on real LilyPond,
paired with the difference Lily# currently shows. See README.md for how to add or
regenerate an entry. The 'lilypond' numbers are DATA: they change only by re-running
the probes in probes/ against lilypond.exe and pasting what it prints.
residual = lilysharp - lilypond, in staff-spaces. A non-zero residual MUST carry a
'why'. Naming the defect is the goal; where it is not yet isolated, say so with an
'OPEN:' prefix and state exactly what is unexplained. What is forbidden is a silent
baseline. Both directions of change are failures: a residual that grows is a
regression, and a residual that shrinks is progress that must be recorded on purpose
so it appears in the diff rather than being absorbed.
The count of exact entries and the total |residual| are the headline fidelity numbers.

barline.next.accidental-to-notehead.why: LilyPond measures the accidental's right SKYLINE against the note heads' skyline (accidental-placement.cc:412), not their boxes, so the gap is padding 0.2 + right-padding 0.15 plus a per-glyph skyline term. Lily# ports the 0.35 and not the skyline, and for a sharp that term is -0.000010 — measured by zeroing both paddings on 2.24.4, which leaves the skyline alone. This is the whole residual. Was -0.149990 while AccidentalNoteGap was LilyPond's `padding` alone with `right-padding` missing.

barline.next.key-change-to-notehead.why: The NATURAL's skyline term, arriving through Paper_column::minimum_distance exactly as the sharp's does in the two entries above — the note opening this measure is a c' under A major, so it carries one, and its reach is the musical column's leftmost ink. A natural is vertically thin, so its right skyline stands 0.017606 further out than its box (measured by zeroing AccidentalPlacement's two paddings on 2.24.4); a sharp's term is 0.000010, which is why this entry is the largest of the three. Same single cause. Was -2.234272 before the boundary column, -0.034272 before the padding.

barline.next.time-change-to-notehead.why: The TimeSignature grob's own width, and the SOURCE of the number is now located: ly:time-signature::print builds a MARKUP and hands it to grob-interpret-markup (scm/time-signature.scm:18-29), and markup text is measured by the text layout engine, not by the music-font path Lily# and the rest of this corpus use. Asked both ways on one and the same grob on 2.24.4: ly:font-get-glyph 'fattened.four' gives 1.600000 while (markup #:number "4") gives 1.604735. So Lily#'s 1.600000 is not a stale or wrong constant — it is exactly what LilyPond's own music-font path reports for that glyph; the two paths simply disagree. Ruled out as the source of 1.604735, for all ten digits: the LILC bbox, the raw outline bounds, the advance, the plain digit family at U+0030-0039 as well as fattened at U+E0B4-U+E0BF, and a font-build difference (LilyPond 2.24.4 ships a different-sized emmentaler-20.otf than the repo copy, but their digit metrics are identical). The markup widths group 0/2/8 at 1.468162, 3/5/7 at 1.331589 and 6/9 at 1.365732, a grouping no metric in the font file reproduces, and a two-digit string is not the concat of two one-digit widths (off by 0.102430 either way) — both consistent with a shaped text run. Closing this needs that text pipeline's metrics, not a constant. The 1.600000 rides through Staff_spacing untouched (the space-alist ideal binds here, not the 0.3 + min_dist correction), so the residual is exactly the width difference. Was -1.454735 before the boundary column existed.

midmeasure.key-cancel.key-to-next-note.why: The same sharp's skyline term as barline.next.accidental-to-notehead, reaching this gap through Paper_column::minimum_distance: the accidental on the next note lifts the rod above the space-alist ideal, so staff-spacing.cc:213 decides the gap as 0.3 + rod and the term rides in with it. That the two entries agree to the digit is what identifies them as one cause. Was -0.149990.
